Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in professional services. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

CRM and intake

Holds enquiries, contacts, opportunities and consent records. Intake, routing and proposal workflows read from it and write back to it.

  • HubSpot
  • Zoho CRM
  • Salesforce
  • Website and Typeform forms

Practice and matter management

The system of record for matters and engagements: parties, staffing, dates and status. Conflict checks, hearing diaries and compliance calendars build on it.

  • Clio
  • PracticePanther
  • In-house matter registers
  • CA practice management tools

Document management and storage

Stores drafts, precedents, client documents and signed letters. Assembly and knowledge workflows inherit its folder structure and permissions.

  • iManage
  • NetDocuments
  • SharePoint
  • Google Drive

Delivery and creative tools

Tracks tasks, review rounds and milestones for agencies and consultancies. Status reports and approval loops draw from it.

  • Jira
  • Asana
  • ClickUp
  • Figma
  • Canva

Accounting and billing

Issues GST invoices and records receipts. Billing workflows draft invoices for approval and read payment status before sending reminders.

  • Tally Prime
  • Zoho Books
  • Busy
  • Razorpay payment links

Government and court portals

Official sources for filings, notices, case status and cause lists. Staff confirm dates and download notices from them; workflows take over from there and never file on a client's behalf.

  • Income tax e-filing portal
  • GST portal
  • MCA21
  • TRACES
  • eCourts Services

Messaging and collaboration

Carries reminders and updates to clients who opted in, and alerts to staff. Client templates are approved in advance, and ID numbers or statements are never requested in chat.

  • WhatsApp Business Platform
  • Email
  • Slack
  • Microsoft Teams

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

First meaningful response time

Elapsed working time from a valid enquiry arriving to a relevant reply from a person, or an approved acknowledgement with clear next steps.

Why it matters: Prospective clients often approach several firms at once; a prompt, relevant reply signals how the firm will treat them as clients.

Time to acceptance decision

Working days from a complete intake form to a recorded conflict, independence or KYC decision by the responsible partner.

Why it matters: Shows whether risk checks are thorough without holding up urgent work, and whether every decision is evidenced.

Proposal or engagement turnaround

Working days from a scoping call or cleared intake to the proposal, statement of work or engagement letter being sent.

Why it matters: Slow turnaround loses competitive bids and leaves work starting without agreed written terms.

Document completeness by cut-off

Share of clients whose required documents are received and verified by the firm's internal cut-off date for the season.

Why it matters: A strong early signal of whether returns and audits will be finished calmly or squeezed into the days before the due date.

Deadlines met with reviewer sign-off

Share of statutory filings, hearing preparations and notice responses completed and reviewed before the internal deadline.

Why it matters: Missed dates are the most damaging and least visible failure in professional services.

Status reports sent on schedule

Share of client status reports sent on the agreed day after review by the account or engagement lead.

Why it matters: Regular, accurate updates reduce escalations and show clients what their retainer or engagement is delivering.

Billable utilization

Billable hours recorded divided by available hours for the period, using the codes and definitions agreed by each practice.

Why it matters: Central to staffing, hiring and pricing decisions in firms that sell professional time.

Realization

Fees billed or collected compared with the value of time recorded at standard rates for the same work.

Why it matters: Shows where scope creep, write-downs or underpricing reduce what recorded time is actually worth.

Days from work done to invoice

Average days between work being performed or a billing milestone being reached and the invoice being issued.

Why it matters: Delayed billing slows cash flow and makes fees harder to collect.

AI answers with valid citations

Share of reviewed knowledge-assistant and research answers whose claims are supported by the cited firm or public sources.

Why it matters: Professionals can rely only on answers they can check; this shows whether the assistant earns that trust.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
